Billy Is a Dog-Friendly Fiat Ducato Camper Van Made for Easygoing Adventures
19 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions
Meet Billy, a mobile home based on an L4H3 Fiat Ducato Maxi. It's the latest project made by Vanlife Conversions, an Essex, UK-based company that, as its name suggests, specializes in camper van conversions.
Billy was built for clients who love traveling and bringing their dogs along for the adventure. You'll definitely see that reflected in the interior design. Before we peek inside, let's see what the van sports on the outside.
You can tell straight away when laying eyes on the van that it's meant for adventuring. For starters, the vehicle rides on black Rogue Alloy wheels wrapped in General Grabber all-terrain tires.
Beyond the wheel and tire combo, another element reveals the fact that the van is meant to go off the beaten path. The lower part of the van was coated in Raptor truck bed liner to provide extra protection against stone chips and scratches.
At the rear, you'll come across a swing-away Thule bike rack for two bikes, attached to the hitch receiver.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions Other notable mods are power and water hookups, a small powered step by the sliding door, a 540 W solar array, and a Thule Omnistor awning.
Enter, and a roomy, beautifully designed interior will welcome you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas for more privacy and better insulation. Above it, you'll come across a large headliner compartment.
The passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van. Even better, you can use it as part of a simple seating area, as you can attach a Lagun table to a mount on the B-pillar by the entrance.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for white laminated cabinetry, white walls, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and a slatted wood ceiling. The look is complemented by bright orange elements, like the curtain and couch cushion upholstery, and a blue subway tile backsplash.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions Dead ahead as you step inside, Vanlife Conversions added a bathroom behind a tall standard door. It boasts a shower with a mixer and a handheld wand, a wall niche for shampoos and soaps, and a removable Nature's Head composting toilet. I love its look, with white subway tile walls and a teak shower mat.
Next, we have the kitchen on the driver's side. It features a 100-liter Indel B fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, a single-burner induction stovetop, and a deep sink with a pull-out faucet. Three overhead cabinets, three drawers, and two lower cabinets are available for storage.
A simple but comfy seating area sits opposite the kitchen. It has two benches facing one another with a Lagun swivel table in the middle. The best part about this area is that it can be transformed into a small bed – you just have to use the table to connect the benches, and then rearrange the cushions.
The rear part of the living space offers the perfect setup for relaxing or sleeping after a long day in nature. You'll discover a bed arranged east to west that measures 190 centimeters (74 inches) in length.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions The bedroom also features three overhead cabinets and two reading lights. A nice touch is that you can leave the rear doors open for a breeze of fresh air, but you can close two curtains to have some privacy.
Alternatively, you can open two small windows integrated into the rear doors, and turn on the ceiling Maxxair vent fan above the bed to create a draft. The latter can be set up to either extract air out or blow air in.
Finally, the part of the van underneath the bedroom was turned into the garage. It offers a bit of storage space and accommodates part of the utility systems in two boxes on the sides. Moreover, it doubles as a bedroom for the dogs, as it has a dog crate that's accessible from the living space through a pass-through.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 460 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging via the alternator while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vanlife Conversions As for plumbing, the van is equipped with an 83-liter (22-gallon) freshwater tank, an under-mounted 62-liter (16-gallon) greywater tank, an outdoor shower connection, and a reverse osmosis water filter.
The builders made one more dog-related modification to the van. They added hooks outside the van, bolted to the vehicle's underside, which allow you to tie a long leash for the dog.
All in all, Billy by Vanlife Conversions shows us just how practical a small space can become provided you use the right design. I'm sure both the customer and their furry friend will make lots of amazing memories in this camper van.
